quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. No one is allowed to pass from either direction.

questions.question: When a traffic light is red but shows a green arrow, when can you go in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in the correct lane for a green arrow, you can go in that direction when the way is clear. This is true even if the red light is still on.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes, what does this mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: What do yellow lines on a road separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. Broken yellow lines mean you can pass only if it is safe.

questions.question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Wait for traffic and pedestrians to clear, then go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Do not go until the lights stop flashing.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel at exactly this speed.
The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at this speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the highest speed allowed on this road. In bad weather or unsafe conditions, you must drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: A red curb means you cannot stop, stand, or park there.

questions.question: Should you treat a railroad crossbuck sign the same as a yield sign?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A railroad crossbuck sign is a yield sign. You must give the right-of-way to any trains and railroad equipment.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross carefully.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass the car ahead when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and let other traffic go first.
Slow down, get ready to stop, and let other traffic pass if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, get ready to stop, and let other traffic pass if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Be ready to stop. Let any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What should you do if your gas pedal gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If the gas pedal sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral right away and press the brake steadily. Drive safely to the side of the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you and you want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming car must stop for you.
Honk to tell the pedestrian to move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: It is safer to handle one hazard at a time. If an oncoming car is approaching, slow down and let it pass. Then pass the pedestrian when it is safe.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: Strong black coffee will keep them awake.
They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
Opening a window and playing loud music will keep them alert.
Only older drivers get drowsy.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear to be drunk. Coffee, open windows, and loud music are not enough to make a drowsy driver truly alert.

questions.question: When you leave a curb to enter traffic, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a big enough gap so you can speed up to match other cars.
Wait for two cars to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a big enough gap so you can speed up to match other cars.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a large enough gap. This gap should allow your car to speed up to the same speed as the other traffic.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: Which of these distractions increases crash risk the most?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you and increase crash risk. Even hands-free phones are dangerous distractions.

questions.question: What can bad suspension cause?

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your car and ride smoothly. If your car bounces a lot over bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often, to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a car is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often, to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors often while driving. This helps you know where cars are near you.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake hard and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tight and use the brakes gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and use the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out while driving, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using the brakes gently. Do not stop on the road. Pull off the road to a safe place.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, what should you turn on so other drivers can see you?

options.text: Turn up the dashboard lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Always use low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, how can you ensure safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to ride home with a friend who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol's effects. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get in front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass another car, there is a higher risk of a crash. If you drive faster than traffic around you, you will pass more cars. Drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass if there is oncoming traffic, if a curve or hill blocks your view, at an intersection, at a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in any no-passing zone. Never pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate that is being raised or lowered at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if your car will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution and cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Be aware of vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must keep to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are moving slower than traffic around you. On interstates, you cannot back up or make U-turns, so go to the next exit if you miss yours.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull onto the shoulder and stop until the rain lets up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: After an accident, do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make injuries worse. Keep them warm while waiting for help. If there is heavy bleeding, use direct pressure to slow it down.

questions.question: When driving, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At a stop sign.
At a red light.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop in these situations: at a stop sign, at a red light, or whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other cars?

options.text: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes. It is good defensive driving.
Yes. It is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Slow down in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can be ticketed.

questions.question: An intersection has no signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a car to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other car stop.
Honk and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two cars reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for that car to pass safely before you go.
